title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the notes compute the 'absolute cohomology' of the Tate motive. Rationally this is étale cohomology of G_m shifted by one, i.e. Z(1) ~ G_m[-1]. The previous page computes H^i(Ū, G_m) and H^i(X, Q(1)) for curves; the next page is headed 'calcul de cohomologie absolue du motif de Tate Z(n)'. This page proves a general lemma: for X integral and locally factorial, H^i(X, G_m) is torsion for i >= 2, so H^i(X, Q(1)) is concentrated in low degrees.

Step 1. Reduce to X irreducible with generic point y, and let j = i_y : y -> X.

Step 2. Take the Leray spectral sequence for étale cohomology: E_2^{pq} = H^p(X, R^q j_* G_m) => H^{p+q}(y, G_m).
- For q > 0, H^q(y, G_m) is Galois cohomology of the function field. It vanishes for q = 1 (Hilbert 90) and is torsion for q >= 2.
- The stalks of R^q j_* G_m are Galois cohomology of fraction fields of strict henselizations, hence torsion for q > 0.
- Working modulo the Serre class of torsion groups, the edge map gives H^p(X, j_* G_m) ≅ H^p(y, G_m) mod torsion. So H^p(X, R*_X) is torsion for p > 0, where R*_X = j_* G_{m,y} is the étale sheaf of nonzero rational functions.
- This identification is stated to hold when X has no embedded primes ('sans idéaux premiers immergés').

Step 3. Use the exact sequence (5.1.1): 0 -> G_{m,X} -> R*_X -> Div_X -> 0, with Div_X the étale sheaf of Cartier divisors. The long exact sequence shows that the boundary map ∂ : H^i(X, Div_X) -> H^{i+1}(X, G_m) is bijective mod torsion for i >= 1.

Step 4 (broken off). Factoriality is to give an isomorphism of étale sheaves Div_X ≅ ⊕_{x of codim 1} i_{x*} Z (Cartier = Weil). Then H^i(X, Div_X) is built from H^i(k(x), Z) = H^{i-1}(k(x), Q/Z), which is torsion for i >= 1, together with higher direct images that are again torsion. The conclusion is that H^{i}(X, G_m) ⊗ Q = 0 for i >= 2. Equivalently, H^i(X, Q(1)) = H^{i-1}(X, G_m) ⊗ Q vanishes for i >= 3 in this generality. The margin note 'Démontrer la conclusion 5.9' indicates this lemma feeds a numbered statement 5.9.

This is the same argument as Grothendieck's proof that Br(X), and more generally H^i(X, G_m) for i >= 2, is torsion for X regular (Groupe de Brauer II, §1).
errors: Gap: identifying R*_X = j_* G_{m,y} with the sheaf of invertible meromorphic functions, and the exactness of 0 -> G_m -> R* -> Div -> 0 étale-locally, needs X reduced without embedded primes; the author flags this. To identify Div_X with Weil divisors étale-locally one needs strict henselizations factorial (or X regular), not just Zariski-local factoriality. The text says 'hypothèse de factorialité' without specifying 'strict'.

Statement precision: the curve case on the previous page, H^3(X, Q(1)) = Q, refers to H^2(X, G_m) ⊗ Q in a non-étale (absolute or Weil-type) sense, or to a different normalization. It is in tension with this page's conclusion that H^{i}(X, G_m) ⊗ Q = 0 for i >= 2 for étale cohomology of regular X. Presumably the notes use a modified absolute cohomology, but this is not explicit on the page.

ideas.what: Leray spectral sequence for j: generic point -> X shows H^p(X, j_*G_m) is torsion for p > 0
ideas.modern_name: Torsion of higher cohomology of the sheaf of rational functions
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer II, §1 (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas)

ideas.what: Exact sequence 0 -> G_m -> j_*G_m -> Div -> 0 and Div ≅ ⊕ i_{x*}Z for locally factorial X, giving H^i(X, G_m) torsion for i >= 2
ideas.modern_name: Br(X) and H^{i>=2}(X, G_m) are torsion for regular X
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer II, Prop. 1.4 and surrounding

ideas.what: Using étale G_m-cohomology tensored with Q as absolute (motivic) cohomology of the Tate motive Q(1), i.e. Z(1) ~ G_m[-1]
ideas.modern_name: Motivic complex Z(1) ≅ G_m[-1]; absolute/motivic cohomology
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; possibly echoed in letters on motives (unsure)

missed.claim: Historical: in notes on a Galois theory of motives, Grothendieck frames étale cohomology of G_m (rationalized, shifted) as the 'absolute cohomology of the Tate motive Z(1)'. This anticipates the later identification Z(1) = G_m[-1] in Lichtenbaum–Beilinson motivic cohomology. The mathematics on this page itself is the published Brauer II argument.
missed.quote: calcul de cohomologie absolue du motif de Tate Z(n)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early (1965 or c. 1977) Grothendieck use of 'absolute cohomology' of Tate motives, relevant to the prehistory of motivic cohomology and the Beilinson conjectures. It is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page reproduces the standard argument from Groupe de Brauer II that higher G_m-cohomology of regular schemes is torsion. The only notable aspect is the framing as absolute cohomology of the Tate motive, which is historically interesting but not mathematically new.

'[-... des les groupes-] {+est un gp de torsion pour p>0,+}' refers to H^p(X, R*_X) being a torsion group for p > 0.
